newsitem.title: UK: Israel says hopes for quick Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel says hopes for quick Hebron deal.

text.p: Israel hopes that it can reach a quick agreement with Palestinians on a long-overdue troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Wednesday.

"Our government will continue the peace process. I hope we will have an agreement in a very short time on Hebron," Mordechai told reporters in London after meeting British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday that further delays in negotiations on Hebron would pose a direct threat to the Middle East peace process. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses Arafat of holding up the talks.

The talks on Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians, are stalemated over Netanyahu's insistence his troops be allowed to enter parts of the city under PLO control in "hot pursuit" of suspected guerrillas.

"I believe that everywhere in Israel people have a right to live in holy places. Hebron is a holy place to the Jews and the Arabs. We respect the Palestinians in the area and they have to respect the Jews," Mordechai said.
Netanyahu wants to modify security arrangements agreed in a partial pullout deal signed with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) by its previous Labour-led government.
